title_en: Fuchun Shipping Co., Ltd. and Shengwei Shipping Co., Ltd. v. Angang Group International Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. — retrial of dispute over delivery of goods without original bills of lading in maritime transport

full_text_en:
Fuchun Navigation Co., Ltd. and Shengwei Navigation Co., Ltd.  
v.  
Angang Group International Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. — Retrial of Dispute over Delivery of Goods without Original Bills of Lading in Maritime Transport  

Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China  
Civil Judgment  

(2000) Jiaoti Zi No. 6  

Applicants for Retrial: Fuchun Navigation Co., Ltd. (WOODTRANS NAVIGATION CORPORATION, PANAMA). Domicile: 53rd Street, Urbanizacion Obarrio, Torre Bancosur, 16th Floor, Panama City, Republic of Panama.  

Legal Representative: Zhang Yiqiang (Mr. Tiong Ngie-Kiang), Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company.  

Authorized Agent: Tong Mei, attorney at Haitong Law Firm.  

Authorized Agent: Yang Wengui, attorney at Haitong Law Firm.  

Applicants for Retrial: Shengwei Navigation Co., Ltd. (SANWAI NAVIGATION S.A., PANAMA). Domicile: 6th Floor, No. 276, Guangfu South Road, Taipei City, China.  

Legal Representative: Lin Qingchi, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company.  

Authorized Agent: Tong Mei, attorney at Haitong Law Firm.  

Authorized Agent: Yang Wengui, attorney at Haitong Law Firm.  

Original Respondent at Second Instance: Angang Group International Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 322, South Zhonghua Road, Anshan City, Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China.  

Legal Representative: Liu Wangjie, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company.  

Authorized Agent: Wang Pengnan, Professor, School of Law, Dalian Maritime University.  

Fuchun Navigation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fuchun) and Shengwei Navigation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shengwei), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (1997) Liao Jing Zhong Zi No. 39 of the Liaoning High People's Court in the dispute with Angang Group International Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Angang) over delivery of goods without original bills of lading in maritime transport, filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court, on October 8, 2000, ruled to conduct a retrial of this case on the grounds that the original judgment contained errors in fact-finding and improper application of law. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing of this case. Lin Qingchi, the legal representative of Shengwei; Tong Mei, the authorized agent of Fuchun and Shengwei; and Wang Pengnan, the authorized agent of Angang, attended the proceedings. This case is now concluded.  

The original judgment found: On February 20, 1995, Angang entered into a sales contract with Hong Kong Qianjinyi Company (hereinafter referred to as Qianjinyi), whereby Angang was to supply Qianjinyi with 5,000 tons of hot-rolled coils at USD 295 per ton, on FOB terms, with payment by letter of credit. On June 30 of the same year, the vessel "UNISON PRAISE," owned by Fuchun, loaded the cargo under the above contract at Dalian Port. After loading, the carrier Mopati Shipping Company (hereinafter referred to as Mopati) issued a full set of three original bills of lading to Angang. The bill of lading indicated: shipper as Angang, consignee as per order of Bank Bumi Daya Private Bank, Said Branch, Jakarta; port of loading as Dalian; port of discharge as Jakarta; cargo weight 5,155.520 tons. On July 21, the "UNISON PRAISE" arrived at Jakarta Port. After the cargo was discharged, the carrier delivered the cargo to the notify party named on the bill of lading without receiving the original bill of lading. Angang, upon receiving the issued clean on-board bill of lading, submitted the full set of documents, including the original bill of lading and commercial invoice, through the Bank of China Anshan Branch to the issuing bank for negotiation. The commercial invoice showed the total value of the goods as USD 1,520,878.40. The above documents were forwarded to the issuing bank on July 8. Due to discrepancies in the letter of credit, the issuing bank returned the full set of documents. Angang received the returned bill of lading and invoice on August 20.  

Fuchun is the registered owner of the carrying vessel "UNISON PRAISE." The vessel "UNISON GREAT," detained by the Dalian Maritime Court, is a sister ship of the "UNISON PRAISE" and is owned by Fuchun. On April 16, 1996, Fuchun sold the "UNISON GREAT" to Shengwei, which renamed the vessel "SANWAI." The Public Registry of the Republic of Panama confirmed that the ownership of the "UNISON GREAT" had not been deregistered, and the owner of the vessel remained Fuchun.  

The Dalian Maritime Court held: From the time the carrier Mopati issued the bill of lading and delivered the cargo to the "UNISON PRAISE," owned by Fuchun, for carriage, Fuchun assumed the legal status of an actual carrier in law. A bill of lading is, by law, evidence of the contract of carriage of goods by sea, a document of title to the goods stated therein, and a document by which the carrier guarantees to deliver the goods. When the shipper holds the bill of lading, the rights and obligations between the carrier and the holder of the bill of lading shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the bill of lading. According to legal provisions, delivery of goods against the original bill of lading is a statutory duty of the carrier. Pursuant to Article 61 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Maritime Code), delivery of goods against the original bill of lading is also a duty of the actual carrier. In the case of a time charter, although Article 136 of the Maritime Code grants the charterer the right to give instructions to the master regarding the operation of the ship, the instruction given by the carrier in the name of the charterer to the master to deliver the goods without the original bill of lading in this case not only exceeded the lawful rights of the charterer but also violated the mandatory obligation imposed by law on the carrier and the actual carrier to deliver goods against the original bill of lading. Fuchun, knowing that delivering goods against the original bill of lading was its mandatory duty, nevertheless insisted on delivering the goods without the original bill of lading. This was a knowing and intentional illegal act. As such, Fuchun is not entitled to the exemptions or limitations of liability under the bill of lading and shall bear full civil liability for Angang's losses. Additionally, the Dalian Maritime Court held that the "SANWAI" operated under the Panamanian flag. Pursuant to Article 270 of the Maritime Code, the determination of the ownership of the "SANWAI" (formerly the "UNISON GREAT") at the time of its detention shall be governed by Panamanian law. According to Article 1083, paragraph 1, of the Panamanian Maritime Code, the transfer of ownership of a vessel can only be asserted against third parties after registration with the Public Registry. Article 1089 further provides that, in any case, the transfer of ownership can only be asserted against third parties after registration with the Public Registry. Although the third party Shengwei purchased the "UNISON GREAT" from Fuchun, at the time the Dalian Maritime Court detained the vessel, Fuchun had not completed the formalities for the transfer of ownership of the vessel with the Panamanian Public Registry. Therefore, the vessel was still owned by Fuchun at the time of the court-ordered detention. The objection raised by the third party Shengwei, claiming to be the lawful owner of the vessel, was untenable. Accordingly, the court ordered Fuchun to compensate Angang for the loss of the cargo value in the amount of RMB 12,700,000, plus interest at a monthly rate of 10.98% from August 20, 1995, until the date of payment; and dismissed the claim of the third party Shengwei regarding the ownership of the "SANWAI" and its request for Angang to bear liability for wrongful arrest of the vessel.  

After the first-instance judgment, Fuchun and Shengwei, dissatisfied, appealed to the Liaoning High People's Court. The Liaoning High People's Court held: Angang is the holder of the original bill of lading. Its right to claim compensation for economic losses from Fuchun for delivering goods without the original bill of lading shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Maritime Code and international shipping practices, be protected by law. Although Fuchun had entered into a time charter party with Mopati, and the delivery of goods without the original bill of lading in this case occurred while the "UNISON PRAISE," owned by Fuchun, was performing under that time charter party, Fuchun cannot thereby be exempted from its statutory civil obligations. From the time the "UNISON PRAISE" carried the cargo under the bill of lading in this case, its owner Fuchun assumed the status of an actual carrier. Delivering goods against the original bill of lading is a statutory duty and obligation not only of the carrier but also of the actual carrier. By delivering the goods to the notify party named on the bill of lading without the original bill of lading, Fuchun shall bear full civil liability for Angang's losses. The "UNISON PRAISE," owned by Fuchun, should have constrained its conduct in accordance with legal provisions and international shipping practices. Its compliance with the carrier's instruction to deliver goods without the bill of lading, while entitling it to claim recourse against the party giving the instruction for economic losses, does not constitute a lawful condition for its exemption from liability. Fuchun's grounds for appeal were not sustainable. Shengwei's grounds for appeal raised objections to the pre-trial arrest of the vessel. The facts and evidence concerning the preservation measures during the original trial had been fully investigated; its objections lacked factual and legal basis. Shengwei had no legal interest in the dispute over compensation for delivery of goods without the original bill of lading and did not have an independent claim as provided by law. These grounds for appeal could not be adopted. The court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the original judgment.  

The grounds for the retrial application by Fuchun and Shengwei were: The original judgment erred in finding that Fuchun participated in the delivery of goods without the bill of lading. Mopati was the time charterer. On July 8, 1995, it issued a clean on-board bill of lading. The bill of lading dated June 30, as found by the original judgment, was an ante-dated bill of lading issued at the request of the shipper, who needed to meet the requirements of the letter of credit, to the ship agent Dalian Penavico, appointed by the time charterer Mopati. Since there was a charter party between Fuchun and Mopati, and the bill of lading was issued by Mopati, the delivery of goods without the bill of lading was not the fault of the shipowner. The shipper's loss was not caused by the actual carrier. The bill of lading issued by the contractual carrier Mopati was retrieved after discharge. The bill of lading held by Angang was an ante-dated bill of lading issued by Mopati's agent. The carrier had completed the carriage and retrieved the bill of lading, and was not at fault. When the "SANWAI" was arrested at Shanghai Port, the vessel had obtained a provisional certificate of nationality, the documents for the sale and transfer of the vessel had been notarized, and the registration with the Panamanian Public Registry had been filed. Based on a correct understanding of Panamanian maritime law, ownership had already been transferred to Shengwei.  

Angang argued in its defense: Fuchun illegally issued a bill of lading to the buyer (charterer) of the goods, thereby depriving Angang (the shipper) of its ownership of the goods, fundamentally breaching the contract of carriage of goods by sea, and should therefore bear legal liability for delivering goods without the original bill of lading. In this case, the actual carrier, Fuchun, as the owner of the carrying vessel, directly participated in issuing the original bill of lading to the intermediate trader (buyer) Qianjinyi. In the context of a time charter, the shipowner, as the actual carrier, shall bear joint and several liability for losses caused to the shipper by issuing a bill of lading to a non-shipper (the buyer). The arrest of the "SANWAI" was correct.  

This Court finds upon retrial: On February 20, 1995, Angang entered into a sales contract with Qianjinyi, whereby Angang was to supply Qianjinyi with 5,000 tons of hot-rolled coils at USD 295 per ton, on FOB terms, with payment by letter of credit. During the period when the "UNISON PRAISE," owned by Fuchun, was time-chartered to Mopati, it loaded the cargo under the above contract at Dalian Port on July 8, 1995, in accordance with the voyage charter party between Mopati and Qianjinyi. On July 9, 1995, the cargo was loaded. The mate's receipt issued by Dalian Penavico was dated July 9, 1995, and contained remarks: cargo rusted, coils loose with damaged bands. On the same day, Mopati's agent, Dalian Penavico, upon Angang's issuance of a letter of indemnity, issued a full set of three original bills of lading dated June 30, 1995, to Angang. The bill of lading indicated: shipper as Angang, consignee as per order of Bank Bumi Daya Private Bank, Said Branch, Jakarta; port of loading as Dalian; port of discharge as Jakarta; cargo weight 5,155.520 tons.  

While the "UNISON PRAISE" was loading cargo at Dalian Port, Mopati, on July 8, 1995, issued a bill of lading to Qianjinyi upon Qianjinyi's issuance of a letter of indemnity. The place of issuance of this bill of lading was Dalian. Qianjinyi's letter of indemnity was addressed to: Owners/Agents/Carriers/Master of the "UNISON PRAISE." The letter of indemnity stated: "In consideration of your delivering to us or to our order a second set of bills of lading... without presentation of the first set of bills of lading..."  

On July 21, the "UNISON PRAISE" arrived at Jakarta Port. After the cargo was discharged, the consignee provided a bank guarantee to Mopati. Pursuant to Mopati's instructions, and based on the bank guarantee and a copy of the bill of lading issued by Mopati to Qianjinyi on July 8, the "UNISON PRAISE" delivered the cargo to the consignee. The original bill of lading dated July 8 was subsequently recovered. That bill of lading had been negotiated through banks and endorsed by the order party.  

After obtaining the clean bill of lading issued by Dalian Penavico on behalf of the carrier Mopati, Angang submitted the full set of documents, including the original bill of lading and commercial invoice, through the advising bank, Bank of China Anshan Branch, to the issuing bank for negotiation. The commercial invoice showed the total value of Angang's goods as USD 1,520,878.40. The above documents were forwarded to the issuing bank on July 18. Due to discrepancies in the letter of credit, the issuing bank returned the full set of documents. Angang received the returned bill of lading and invoice on August 20.  

Angang filed a lawsuit against Fuchun and Mopati in the Dalian Maritime Court, seeking compensation for losses caused by the delivery of goods without the original bill of lading and applying for property preservation. The Dalian Maritime Court arrested the "SANWAI" (formerly the "UNISON GREAT"), owned by Fuchun, at Shanghai Port on May 6, 1996. On May 17, Shengwei filed an objection with the court, claiming ownership of the arrested "SANWAI." The Dalian Maritime Court notified it to participate in the proceedings as a third party. On May 31, the People's Insurance Company of China, on behalf of the Japan Ship Owners' Protection & Indemnity Association, provided a guarantee of USD 1.8 million to the court for the owner of the arrested vessel, and the court lifted the arrest.  

During the first-instance trial, Angang withdrew its claim against Mopati.  

The above facts are supported by the following evidence: the original bill of lading issued by Mopati to Qianjinyi on July 8, 1995; the original bill of lading issued by Dalian Penavico to Angang on July 9, 1995; the letter of indemnity issued by Angang to Dalian Penavico to obtain a clean bill of lading; the letter of indemnity issued by Qianjinyi to obtain the bill of lading dated July 8, 1995; the consignee's letter of indemnity for taking delivery of the goods; the mate's receipt from Dalian Penavico; the civil ruling of the court for the arrest of the vessel; and the trial transcript.  

This Court holds: This case is a dispute over delivery of goods without original bills of lading in maritime transport brought by Angang against Fuchun. During the first and second instance proceedings, the parties did not object to the application of Chinese maritime law, so it is determined that Chinese law applies to this case.  

Pursuant to Article 270 of the Maritime Code, the acquisition, transfer, and extinction of ownership of a vessel shall be governed by the law of the flag state. Regarding the ownership of the "SANWAI" in this case, the relevant laws of the Republic of Panama shall apply. According to the findings of the original trial court, at the time the Dalian Maritime Court arrested the "SANWAI," Fuchun had not completed the formalities for the transfer of ownership of the vessel with the Public Registry. Therefore, Shengwei's assertion that ownership of the vessel had already been transferred to Shengwei at the time of the arrest lacks sufficient basis and is not supported.  

The bill of lading on which Angang based its lawsuit was issued by Dalian Penavico, the agent of Mopati, who was the time charterer of the "UNISON PRAISE." The bill of lading was Mopati's bill of lading, and the bill of lading clearly indicated the carrier as Mopati. Therefore, in accordance with the provisions of the Maritime Code, Fuchun, as the owner of the carrying vessel "UNISON PRAISE," having entered into a time charter party with the carrier Mopati and actually performed the carriage, shall be deemed the actual carrier for this voyage of maritime cargo transport. Angang, suing Fuchun on this bill of lading in a dispute over a contract of carriage of goods by sea, has a right of action. However, in the transportation of the goods involved in this case, in addition to the aforementioned bill of lading, the carrier Mopati also issued a bill of lading to Qianjinyi, the charterer under the voyage charter party. After the cargo arrived at the port of destination, the person taking delivery provided a bank guarantee to Mopati. Pursuant to Mopati's instructions, and based on the bank guarantee and a copy of the bill of lading issued by Mopati to Qianjinyi, the ship delivered the cargo to the person taking delivery and subsequently recovered the original bill of lading issued by Mopati to Qianjinyi. According to the available evidence, the agents at both the loading port and the discharging port were appointed by the carrier Mopati, and according to the terms of the time charter party, regarding matters related to ship operation, the ship was to follow the charterer's instructions. Therefore, Angang's assertion that Fuchun participated in the delivery of goods without the original bill of lading lacks sufficient basis. Consequently, the original judgment's finding that the shipowner Fuchun bore responsibility for the delivery of goods without the original bill of lading in this case lacks factual and legal basis.  

Angang's assertion that Fuchun actually accepted the letter of indemnity issued by Qianjinyi to apply for the issuance of the bill of lading and sued Qianjinyi in Hong Kong, thereby claiming that Fuchun participated in the issuance of the bill of lading to Qianjinyi, lacks sufficient basis. This Court does not support this assertion. This case is a dispute between Angang and Fuchun over delivery of goods without original bills of lading in maritime transport, not a dispute over the issuance of bills of lading. Angang's claim during the retrial that its loss was related to the issuance of two sets of bills of lading exceeds the scope of this case's trial. Furthermore, Qianjinyi's letter of indemnity was addressed to the Owners/Agents/Carriers/Master of the "UNISON PRAISE." Based on the actual conduct of issuing the bill of lading by Mopati, it was Mopati, not Fuchun, that accepted the letter of indemnity. As for Fuchun's act of suing Qianjinyi in Hong Kong after Angang filed a lawsuit against it in the Dalian Maritime Court, this cannot prove Fuchun's participation in the issuance of the bill of lading. Fuchun's request to reverse the judgment is in accordance with the law. Angang's assertions lack sufficient basis, and the original judgment should be corrected.  

Pursuant to Article 60, paragraph 1, of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, and Article 179, paragraph 1, items (2) and (3), and Article 184, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:  

1. The civil judgment (1997) Liao Jing Zhong Zi No. 39 of the Liaoning High People's Court is set aside;  
2. The civil judgment (1996) Dahai Fashang Chu Zi No. 72 of the Dalian Maritime Court is set aside;  
3. Angang's claim is dismissed;  
4. The requests of Fuchun and Shengwei regarding the transfer of ownership of the vessel "SANWAI" to Shengwei are dismissed.  

The litigation costs of the first and second instances shall be borne by Angang.  

This judgment is final.  

Presiding Judge: Lei Xuhui  
Judge: Wang Shumei
